chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Hanan, from Muawiya ibn Taref, from Sufyan al-Thawri, who said:

I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about a man who stole a free woman and sold her. He said: 'In her case, there are four penalties (hudud). As for the first, he is a thief, so his hand is cut off. And the second: if he copulated with her, he is whipped the penalty (hadd). And upon the one who bought her: if he copulated with her and knew (she was stolen), if he was married (muhsan), he is stoned; and if he was not married, he is whipped the penalty (hadd). And if he did not know, then there is nothing upon him. And upon her: if he coerced her, then there is nothing upon her; and if she obeyed him, she is whipped the penalty (hadd).'

key_terms.حُرَّةً: Free woman (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: What are the four hudud penalties for stealing and selling a free woman according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the compound legal penalties (hudud) for kidnapping and selling a free woman, demonstrating the Shia jurisprudential principle of applying multiple distinct punishments for a single act when different legal conditions are met. The ruling distinguishes between the thief's hand amputation for the theft itself and the sexual penalties (flogging or stoning) based on marital status and consent, while also clarifying the woman's liability only if she consented to the intercourse. This hadith highlights the precision of Ja'fari fiqh in separating the crime of theft from the crime of unlawful sexual intercourse (zina) within the context of abduction.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Hanan, from Muawiya Bin Tareyf, from Sufyan Al Sowry who said,

‘I asked Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws about a man who stole a free woman, so he sold her. So heasws said: ‘Four Penalties (are applicable) – as for the first one, so he is a thief, his hand would be cut; and the second if he had copulated with her, he would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd), and (a Penalty (Hadd)) upon the one who bought, if he had knowingly copulated with her, if he was married, stoning, and if he was not married, the Penalty (Hadd) of whipping; and if he had not known, then there is nothing upon him; and upon her, if she was coerced (forced), so there is nothing upon her, and if she had obeyed him, she would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd)’.
